title: Patch: a watched game's turn clock counts down, and a finished one stops saying Disconnected
thread: **Issue #2974 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #2974: Patch: a watched game's turn clock counts down, and a finished one stops saying Disconnected Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means When you watch a friend's game, the turn clock shows a number that stays frozen while your friend thinks and jumps when they act, so you cannot tell how long they have left. And when the game ends normally, the status line says "Disconnected" beside the result, as if something broke. Once built, the clock ticks down between updates, silently, and a finished game says it is over. ## Why - `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx:329-344` passes the board no `turnClock`, so `game/Board.tsx:787` falls back to a static `formatSeconds(view.clockMs)`. The co-op watch's chrome (`WatchRoute.tsx:319`) has no clock either. - The server fills `clockMs` into every watcher's frame (`crates/server/src/actor/match_actor.rs:828-839`, recorded by `spectate_record_in`, 2889-2897), so the number is there to count from. A player's own board ticks (`routes/match.tsx:513`, `game/Clock.tsx`). - A finished game's socket closing sets the status to closed (`WatchRoute.tsx:185-187`), which reads "Disconnected" (lines 229-230), though the comment at line 270 already knows a finished game's socket closes as closed too. ## Proposal - A small read-only countdown from each frame's `clockMs`, ticking from the frame's arrival, with no alarm, sound or haptic (the player's `Clock` plays the turn alarm, which a watcher must not hear). It is passed as `turnClock`, and to the co-op chrome. - When the shown view has a result, the status line reads a finished game's words instead of the connection's. ## Where it lands `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx`, possibly a small component in `apps/web/src/game/`, `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With fake timers, a frame with `clockMs` 60000 followed by 10 s shows 50; a new frame resets it. - [ ] No sound or haptic cue plays from the watched clock. - [ ] A finished frame followed by the socket's close shows no "Disconnected". - [ ] The co-op watch shows the same ticking clock. ## Size and risks Small. The countdown assumes the deadline holds between frames; a prompt or a timeout sends a new frame, which resets it. The board is `SPECTATE_DELAY_MS` behind and the clock is read at the same moment, so the two stay consistent. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41758736592)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal A watched game's turn clock counts down on its own between frames, in both the 1v1 watch and the co-op watch. It counts down silently: no alarm, no sound, no haptic. A frame that carries a result puts a finished game's words ("Game over") in the status line instead of the connection's, so a normal close no longer reads "Disconnected". Each requirement is covered by an acceptance test below. ## Files to touch | File | Change | |---|---| | `apps/web/src/together/WatchClock.tsx` | **new**. `WatchClockReading` type, `watchClockOf(clockMs)`, and the read-only `WatchClock` component. | | `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx` | change. `useWatch` stamps each view frame's `clockMs` and returns `clock`. The status line gets `finished`. `WatchClock` is passed to `Game` as `turnClock` and to the co-op chrome as `clock`. Header comment gets one line. | | `apps/web/src/together/config.ts` | change. Add the constant `WATCH_CLOCK_TICK_MS`. | | `apps/web/src/together/testids.ts` | change. Add `clock: "watch-clock"` to `watchTestid`. | | `e2e/support/testids.ts` | change. Mirror it: `export const WATCH_CLOCK = "watch-clock";` after `WATCH_RECONNECT`. | | `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx` | change. New describe with the acceptance tests. | | `apps/web/README.md` | change. One clause in the `/watch/:matchId` entry (around line 570). | `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` does not change: "Game over" is already an entry (line 7) and the board's own header uses it. Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/` (the server already fills `clockMs`), `game/Clock.tsx`, `game/Board.tsx` or `duos/`. No ruling, no `spec/` edit and no pending patch fragment. This is presentation only and ships no card data (precedent: #2921, which changed only `apps/web/src/together/`). `spec/rulings/R2881000.md` already says a co-op watcher's view carries "the clock's time left as the seat was shown it". That is the number counted down from. ## Steps 1. **`together/config.ts`**: append after `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`: ```ts /** How often a watched game's clock repaints (presentation only, not a SPEC value). */ export const WATCH_CLOCK_TICK_MS = 250; ``` 2. **`together/testids.ts`**: in `watchTestid`, after `reconnect`, add `/** The friend's turn clock, counted down from the newest frame's clockMs (#2974). */ clock: "watch-clock",`. Then add the mirror line to `e2e/support/testids.ts`. 3. **Create `together/WatchClock.tsx`** (copy the tick pattern of `RoundClock` in `duos/DuosRoute.tsx`). - Header comment: the readout counts down a watched frame's `clockMs` from its arrival, silently. It uses no `useTurnClockAlarm` and no haptics. It decides nothing (CLAUDE.md rule 7). - Imports: `useEffect`, `useState`, `type ReactElement` from react; `defaultMonotonic` from `../game/net.ts`; `secondsLeft` from `../game/clockUrgency.ts`; `formatSeconds` and `useLocale` from `../i18n/i18n.ts`; `WATCH_CLOCK_TICK_MS` from `./config.ts`; `watchTestid` from `./testids.ts`. - `export type WatchClockReading = { ms: number; at: number };`. `ms` is the frame's `clockMs`, and `at` is the monotonic reading when the frame arrived. - `export function watchClockOf(clockMs: number | null): WatchClockReading | null` returns `null` for `null`, else `{ ms: clockMs, at: defaultMonotonic() }`. - `export function WatchClock({ reading }: { reading: WatchClockReading | null }): ReactElement | null`: - Call `useLocale();`. - `const [, setTick] = useState(0);` - A `useEffect` keyed on `[reading]`. If `reading === null` it returns `undefined`. Otherwise it runs `window.setInterval(() => { setTick((tick) => tick + 1); }, WATCH_CLOCK_TICK_MS)` and returns a cleanup that calls `window.clearInterval(id)`. - If `reading === null`, return `null`. - Compute `const left = Math.max(0, reading.ms - Math.max(0, defaultMonotonic() - reading.at));`. - Return `{formatSeconds(secondsLeft(left))}`. - It must return the bare `span`, because `board.css` styles `.turn-mechanism > .clock` and `.turn-mechanism-clock`. It must not import `Clock.tsx` or `../audio`. - The anchor lives in `reading`, not in a ref. `DuosBoard` remounts `Game` when the board flips between own and teammate, so a ref anchor would reset the clock on a flip. 4. **`together/WatchRoute.tsx`, `useWatch`**: - Import `WatchClock`, `watchClockOf` and `type WatchClockReading` from `./WatchClock.tsx`. - Add `const [clock, setClock] = useState(null);` beside the other state. - In the co-op branch, after `setCoopView(frame.view);` add `setClock(watchClockOf(frame.view.own.clockMs));`. - In the 1v1 branch, after `setView(frame.view);` add `setClock(watchClockOf(frame.view.clockMs));`. - Add `clock: WatchClockReading | null;` to the return type and `clock` to the returned object. - A new frame always makes a new reading object, so it resets the countdown even when its number repeats. 5. **`WatchRoute`, status line**: - Destructure `clock` from `useWatch`. - After `const shown = ...` add `const finished = shown?.result != null;`. - Change line 271 to `const exhausted = connection === "closed" && !finished;`. - Change line 273 to `... || (connection === "connecting" && !finished);`. - In the status JSX replace `{connectionWords(connection)}` with `{finished ? t("Game over") : connectionWords(connection)}`. - Leave `data-connection={connection}` on the status span and on the root as they are. They carry the raw state, and existing tests read them. 6. **`WatchRoute`, the clock element**: - After `finished`, add `const turnClock = ;`. A finished game shows no clock. The element is never `undefined`, so `Board`'s static `??` fallback is not used. - Co-op: change the provider value to `{{ back: , status, clock: turnClock }}`. - 1v1: add `turnClock={turnClock}` to ``, after `matchStatus={status}`. 7. **`WatchRoute.tsx` header comment**: add one line: the board's turn clock counts down from each frame's `clockMs`, silently, and a finished game's status line says "Game over" (#2974). 8. **`apps/web/README.md`**: in the `/watch/:matchId` entry, after "SPECTATE_DELAY_MS behind;", add "its turn clock counts down silently from each frame's `clockMs` (together/WatchClock.tsx);". 9. **Tests** (below), then run the checks. ## Tests All in `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx`, in a new `describe("#2974 the watched turn clock and a finished game's status", ...)`. Add a helper beside `advance`: ```ts function fakeClockTimers(): void { vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setTimeout", "clearTimeout", "setInterval", "clearInterval", "performance"] }); } ``` `performance` and `setInterval` must be faked, because the clock reads `performance.now()` and ticks on an interval. The file's `afterEach` already restores real timers. Add the imports `setAudioEngineForTests` from `../audio/engine.ts` and `fakeAudioEngine, type FakeAudioEngine` from `../audio/test/fakeAudio.ts`. - `#2974 a frame's clockMs counts down from its arrival and a new frame resets it`: 1. Call `fakeClockTimers()`, `watch()`, `latest().emit("open")`. 2. Send a view frame with `baseView({ viewer: "p1", clockMs: 60 * MS_PER_SECOND })`. Expect `watch-clock` to have text `60s`. 3. `await advance(10 * MS_PER_SECOND)`. Expect `50s` and `data-remaining-ms` `"50000"`. 4. Send a new frame with the same 60000. Expect `60s` (a new frame resets it even with the same number). 5. Advance 1 s, then send a frame with 30000. Expect `30s`. 6. Advance 40 s. Expect `0s` (it floors at zero and shows no negative number). 7. Send a frame with `clockMs: null`. Expect `queryByTestId("watch-clock")` to be null. - `#2974 the watched clock sounds no alarm and buzzes nothing`: 1. In the describe, add `beforeEach` that does `engine = fakeAudioEngine(); setAudioEngineForTests(engine);` and `afterEach` that does `setAudioEngineForTests(null)`. The fake engine's `state()` is `"running"`, so the player's alarm would be audible there. 2. `const vibrate = vi.fn(() => true);` `Object.defineProperty(window.navigator, "vibrate", { configurable: true, value: vibrate });` and `Reflect.deleteProperty(window.navigator, "vibrate")` in a `finally` or `afterEach`. 3. Send a frame with `clockMs: 12 * MS_PER_SECOND`, which is inside the final 30 s. Advance 15 s. 4. Expect `engine.playSfx.mock.calls.filter(([id]) => id === "heartbeat" || id === "clockTick")` to equal `[]`, and `expect(vibrate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. 5. Check that `watch-clock` shows `0s`, so the test proves the clock really ran. - `#2974 a finished game's frame and its socket's close say Game over, never Disconnected`: 1. Call `fakeClockTimers()`, `watch()`, open, and send `baseView({ viewer: "p1", result: { winner: "p1", reason: "concede" }, clockMs: 5000 })`. 2. Expect status text `Game over` and not `Connected`. Expect `queryByTestId("watch-clock")` to be null. 3. `latest().emit("close")`. Expect `Game over`, not `Disconnected`, and `data-connection` `"closed"`. 4. Expect `queryByTestId("watch-reconnect")` to be null. 5. Leave the existing test at line 444 (a running game that gave up still says "Disconnected") unchanged. It guards the other branch. - `#2974 R2881000 a co-op watch shows the same ticking clock and a finished co-op game says Game over`. Use a local `watchCoop()` as in the existing co-op describe, or put this test inside that describe. 1. Call `fakeClockTimers()`, `watchCoop()`, open, and send `{ type: "view", view: { ...duosView(1), own: baseView({ clockMs: 60 * MS_PER_SECOND }) }, legal: [] }`. Expect `watch-clock` to have text `60s`. 2. Advance 10 s. Expect `50s`. 3. Send a frame with `own.clockMs` 30000 and expect `30s`. 4. Send `{ ...duosView(3, { outcome: "win", winner: "a", reason: "concede" }) }`, then `emit("close")`. Expect status `Game over`, not `Disconnected`, and no `watch-clock`. Commands: - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx` - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Clock.test.tsx` (unchanged, regression) - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/i18n/i18n.test.ts src/writing.test.ts src/wording.test.ts` (the "Game over" string is already translated, so these must stay green) - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` - `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/together e2e/support` ## Done when - [ ] Frame `clockMs` 60000 followed by 10 s shows `50s`, and a new frame resets it. - [ ] No alarm (`heartbeat`/`clockTick`) or vibrate call comes from the watched clock. - [ ] A finished frame followed by the socket's close shows "Game over" and no "Disconnected". - [ ] The co-op watch shows the same ticking clock. - [ ] The existing `WatchRoute.test.tsx` tests still pass, line 461's "Disconnected" among them. - [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, the web's typecheck, eslint, and the web tests touched pass. The harness's other checks need no change: no Rust, catalog, spec or `wire/` file moves. - [ ] No new `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `.skip` or `.only`. ## Risks - **Stale frame on a hello answer:** the server answers a watcher's hello (wake probe, reconnect) with the stored view, whose `clockMs` was recorded earlier. The clock then jumps back up until the next frame. The issue accepts that "a new frame resets it", and fixing it needs a server change, so it is out of scope. Do not infer more on the client. - **Paused turn clock:** while the opponent answers a prompt, the friend's `clockMs` is the banked, paused time, and this readout keeps counting it down until the next frame. The issue accepts this. Do not add a client guess from `pending`. A mulligan makes it unreliable, and `routes/match.tsx` must not be imported into the watch chunk. - **Sound:** keep `WatchClock` free of `../audio` and `Clock.tsx`. The player's `Clock` runs `useTurnClockAlarm` for the viewer's own seat, and the watcher's "you" is the friend. - **Fake timers:** under fake timers in jsdom, `waitFor` hangs, so use `advance` and synchronous asserts, as the file's header says. If `performance` is not faked, the clock never moves in tests. - **Hidden information (rule 7):** the clock reads only the `clockMs` already in the delayed view. The screen still sends only its hello. ## Open questions None. Two choices the issue did not settle: - The finished-game words are the existing "Game over" rather than a new string. Rejected: a new key such as "Finished", which would need a zh-CN entry for no gain. - The countdown anchor is stamped in `useWatch` rather than kept in a ref inside the component. Rejected: a ref anchor, which `DuosBoard`'s remount on a board flip would reset. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-11-04T01:58:35Z: Approve ````
